sources.entry: teikei - A web application that maps out community-supported agriculture based on crowdsourced data. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Teikei is a web application and API that maps community-supported agriculture (CSA) initiatives in Germany, Switzerland, and Austria using crowdsourced data.
summary.what_it_does: Teikei is a monorepo with three modules: an API built with Feathers on Express that serves a JSON REST API backed by PostgreSQL, a React/Redux single-page map frontend that uses Leaflet to display CSA locations, and an admin dashboard built with crudl.io for content moderators and administrators. The API also includes a job queue built with node-schedule. The repository uses npm workspaces and lerna, with top-level scripts to run the full stack and work across modules. A development mode runs the database in Docker and seeds test users and data. The README also mentions an embed package and a Dokku-based deployment setup for preview and production environments.
use_cases: find a CSA farm share in Germany, Switzerland or Austria
crowdsourced directory of solidarity farming initiatives
embed a CSA map on another website
moderate and manage CSA listing data via an admin dashboard
self-host a REST API for agricultural initiative listings
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into teikei
Create a root .env file based on .env.sample, then run scripts/link-env.sh
npm run dev (starts API and Map in development mode; requires Docker)
npm run dev:admin (starts API and Admin in development mode)
npm run build (builds all modules for production)
notable: Crowdsourced map of CSA initiatives covering Germany, Switzerland, and Austria
Monorepo with separate API, map, and admin modules sharing one backend
Used by several German-speaking CSA networks named in the README
Development mode seeds test users with superadmin, admin, and user roles
caveats: Requires Node.js 18 or newer, PostgreSQL 9.5 or newer, and Docker for development mode
Deployment instructions are tailored to Dokku and the author's own app names and environments
README sections are partly incomplete (some URLs and clone address are blank)
